cut: v2 build (4 Nov, en only): caption 3 literal ('must go to district heating'), heat tag carries the rule's own qualifier: SUBSTANTIALLY INTO DISTRICT HEATING. v1 stills (3 Nov): RFH Helsinki, papercut, VIRAL cut. Helsinki's City Board adopted its data-centre siting principles on 2 Nov 2026: five possible areas, waste heat into district heating, not in the most valuable nature. Frame 0 is the papercut Helsinki map with five red pins hanging over it; they drop one by one and are named; heat runs from them along pipes into the houses; then Muhos, where the last trees fall and the site's stake goes in afterwards. Map first there, forest first here. Google named plainly (owner, 2 Nov), no logo.
argument: Helsinki decided in public where data centres may go and that their waste heat must warm homes; at Google's Muhos site, about 330 ha of forest was cleared before the assessment.
syntax: '/' breaks a line, [word] is the pop word; in Japanese a space marks a reveal segment and is never drawn

text.en: Helsinki chose / where data / centres may [go].
text.ja: ヘルシンキが / データセンターの / [場所を] 決めた。

captions.source: City of Helsinki news item, 2 Nov 2026, 'Kaupunginhallitus hyväksyi datakeskusperiaatteet' (hel.fi); STT release the same day; Helsingin Uutiset. The City Board adopted the data-centre siting principles, naming five possible areas. Search summaries only: the decision record on paatokset.hel.fi is blocked from here; the wording is from the city's own news item (plan/HS-SCOUT.md, check of 3 Nov 07:16). 'Chose where data centres may go' = the principles say where projects may be sited; the five are possible areas, not approved projects.

text.ja: 地図に / [5つの] 候補地。

captions.source: hel.fi, 2 Nov 2026 (and STT, Helsingin Uutiset, Verkkouutiset): the five possible areas are Heikinlaakso, Malmi, Salmisaari, Östersundom and Myllypuro. The pins stand on each district on an illustrative map; the city's own site boundaries were not seen, so no pin claims a plot. The tag's rule (not in the most valuable nature areas, 'arvokkaimmille luontoalueille') is from the same news item.

text.en: Their waste heat / must go to / district [heating].
text.ja: 排熱は / [家々を] / 暖めること。

captions.source: hel.fi, 2 Nov 2026: the waste heat must be used substantially in the district-heating network (power sufficiency and environmental and vitality effects are also weighed). v2 (4 Nov, built en): the en caption now says it literally ('must go to district heating', owner's choice left open, literal taken); the tag gives the rule's own qualifier, 'used substantially'. The Finnish line says it literally.

text.ja: ムホスでは / 森が [先に] / 消えた。

captions.source: Muhos, northern Finland, Google's planned data-centre site (Tuike Finland represents Google): about 330 ha cleared in 2026, Google's own figure (Fortune 26 Oct; Kainuun Sanomat; MT; the regulator says over 300 ha). LVV (the licensing and supervisory agency), 6 Oct 2026: the preparatory work at Muhos and Kajaani to stop until the environmental impact assessments are done (AFP; Al Jazeera 7 Oct; Kaleva; SSS). The posted film Count the Trees (Doodle 5) rests on the same two facts. 'The forest went first' is the station's line: the clearing came before the assessment, where Helsinki's map came before any building.

post.en: Helsinki's city board named five possible data-centre areas: Heikinlaakso, Malmi, Salmisaari, Östersundom, Myllypuro. Their waste heat must go to district heating. In Muhos, ~330 ha of forest was cleared for Google before the environmental assessment. Map first or forest first?
post.fi: Helsingin kaupunginhallitus nimesi viisi mahdollista datakeskusaluetta: Heikinlaakso, Malmi, Salmisaari, Östersundom, Myllypuro. Hukkalämpö on käytettävä kaukolämpöön. Muhoksella Googlen alueelta hakattiin ~330 ha metsää ennen YVA-arviointia. Ensin kartta vai ensin metsä?
post.ja: ヘルシンキ市参事会が、データセンターの候補地を5か所示した：ヘイキンラークソ、マルミ、サルミサーリ、エステルスンドム、ミュッリュプロ。排熱は地域暖房に使うこと。ムホスでは、Googleの用地で約330ヘクタールの森が環境影響評価の前に伐採された。地図が先か、森が先か？
